answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small deposit that unlocks only after a history of useful, peer-verified work, so spawning fake identities is costly while honest work stays cheap. Like dawn light through a prism, one verifiable record splits into independent checks - stake, reputation, and work history - so a single ember of fraud cannot ignite a network where every claim must pass all three. As each dawn brings new participants, the checks stay the same, and the ember of a fake identity dies out before it can spread.
